name: Make compost
blurb: Kitchen and garden waste into free soil improver. The whole skill is the balance of greens to browns, plus enough air — get those right and it never smells.
gear: A compost bin or a heap in a corner
A store of browns: cardboard, dry leaves, straw
steps: Learn the ratio: roughly equal volumes of greens (kitchen scraps, grass, coffee grounds) and browns (cardboard, dry leaves, straw). Most failed heaps are all greens.
Chop material small — it decomposes far faster.
Layer greens and browns rather than dumping one thing in bulk, and keep a bag of browns beside the bin for every kitchen caddy you add.
Keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge, and covered so rain does not waterlog it.
Turn it every few weeks to add air. Air is what makes it hot and fast rather than slimy and slow.
Harvest from the bottom once it is dark, crumbly and smells of woodland floor.
tips: Smelly and slimy means too many greens and not enough air. Add cardboard and turn it.
No cooked food, meat or dairy in an open heap unless you want rats.
proof: A barrow of dark crumbly compost you made, spread on your own beds.
